notes: Subject swap, on your own GPU. Add a second picture to the Photo Lab — a pose reference and a character reference — and the job switches from repainting to swapping: FLUX Kontext is shown both pictures side by side and told to keep the left one's pose, framing, lighting and background while making the person the one on the right. That is an instruction to an editing model rather than noise applied to a latent, which is why it needs no denoise tuning, no pose LoRAs and no prompt engineering; anything you type is passed along as extra guidance on top of the instruction. Identity comes from the picture, so LoRAs sit that mode out, and picking a character in the dropdown fills the second slot from their first selfie reference automatically. The pair is stitched inside the app so the geometry is exact, and the output comes back in the pose reference's own shape rather than as a side-by-side. Kontext needs its own models on the volume, about 17GB one time: under Your own GPU there is now Check Kontext, which asks the endpoint whether its ComfyUI knows the nodes and whether the model file is present, and Install Kontext, which downloads the model, both text encoders and the VAE into the right folders with the same throwaway-pod installer the LoRAs use.
